mathematics.logical_review: Independent AI-assisted readings of the entire new indexed-domain section and its direct dependencies completed. Three parallel mathematical reviews covered the general-Q Koszul/AS-index/seven-period argument, domain relation-count forcing, normal-family two-periodicity, one-period descent, and the AS3 top-syzygy argument. The final integrated proof was read independently and its notation and choice of period structure were corrected. This is not formalization or external peer review.
mathematics.scope: Over C, all positive connected locally finite two-sided AS4 Z-algebras with primitive jumps (1,1,2,3), a word-quadratic homogeneous presentation, finite finitely-generated projective resolutions of simples, polynomial row/column growth, and Z-domain property. Standard Hilbert series, one-periodicity and noetherianity are conclusions. General n retains its previously stated hypotheses.
checked: Yoneda perfect pairings from finite resolutions and AS duality
Word-Koszulity, constant AS index, exclusion of indices 6,8,9,10, and word-preserving seven-periodicity
Relation projection upper bounds and the seven-row Euler deficit inequality
Finiteness and uniform comparison of word-Hilbert series without assuming noetherianity
Normal degree-two generator family giving an isomorphism of the full Z-algebra with its two-shift
One-periodicity from the subgroup of periods, without assuming commuting period isomorphisms
Word-preserving descent to an AS-regular graded domain
Rogalski-Zhang normal quotient theorem applied in word degree one, with no noetherian hypothesis
AS3 top-syzygy projections and relation preservation without assuming the quotient is a domain
PBW spanning and Hilbert comparison, Ore compatibility equations, reverse construction and noetherianity as a consequence
primary_sources_checked: Rogalski-Zhang, arXiv:1101.1998v2, Lemma 1.1, Corollary 1.2; Lemma 1.3(c) as an alternative route
not_claimed: Every object of Q is a Z-domain
Standard Hilbert series for the non-domain locus
Existence or nonexistence of exact period-seven objects in the non-domain locus
Complete bare indexed-isomorphism orbits of Ore data
Removal of the hypotheses in the general-n theorem
